stability_labels.consistently_elevated: All evaluated configurations classify this period as elevated
stability_labels.not_elevated: All evaluated configurations classify this period as not elevated
stability_labels.insufficient_evidence: Fewer than min_evaluable_configs configurations produced an evaluable result
stability_labels.insufficient_cross_sensor_evidence: Enough configurations were evaluable, but not every required sensor had an evaluable configuration; no cross-sensor agreement label is assigned. See sensor_specific for single-sensor findings.

sensor_specific_labels.elevated: All evaluable configurations of this sensor classify the period as elevated
sensor_specific_labels.not_elevated: All evaluable configurations of this sensor classify the period as not elevated
sensor_specific_labels.insufficient_evidence: This sensor has no evaluable configuration for the period

cross_sensor_rule.evaluable_means: configuration result is consistently_elevated or not_elevated
never_counted_as_agreement: configurations that did not run (n_not_run), e.g. sensor data absent

limitations: Reliability is classification stability across predefined analytical choices, not a calibrated probability of truth.
Configurations are fixed before analysis; do not add post-hoc configurations.
Insufficient evidence does not mean no fire activity; it means the data or baseline do not support a classification.

Insufficient-evidence configurations are never counted as agreement. A period is labelled consistently_elevated or not_elevated only when at least min_evaluable_required configurations produced an evaluable result.

Configurations that share a sensor are not independent (3 MODIS and 2 VIIRS configurations). Cross-sensor agreement labels therefore require at least one evaluable MODIS and one evaluable VIIRS configuration.
sensor_specific findings describe one sensor only and are not cross-sensor agreement. A sensor-specific label can rest on a single configuration.
Disagreement between sensors reflects analytical sensitivity to sensor choice; it does not show which sensor is closer to actual fire occurrence.
